A: Add a line that starts with `BREAKING CHANGE: ` and says `none` when nothing breaks.
Add a body line `Risk: low`, `Risk: medium` or `Risk: high`.
Start the subject line with a lowercase type prefix and a colon, one of `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `chore:`. Nothing may come before the type.
State whether the change was tested with a line `Tested: yes` or `Tested: no`.
The very last line of the message must be the sign-off `Signed-off-by: <author name>`.
Explain the motivation in a body line that starts with `Why: `.
B: Start the subject line with the ticket ID in square brackets, for example `[PAY-311] `. Nothing may come before the bracket.
Record test status as `Tested: yes` or `Tested: no` on its own line.
Describe the change in the body as a bulleted list with at least two bullets that start with `- `.
Say how to revert in a line that starts with `Rollback: `.
Finish the message with a trailer block that contains the line `Refs: <TICKET-ID>`.

relations.reason: A3 requires the subject line to start with a lowercase type prefix like 'feat:', while B1 requires it to start with a ticket ID in square brackets like '[PAY-311]'. No single subject line can start with both.
Both A4 and B2 require recording the test status with a line 'Tested: yes' or 'Tested: no'.

A5 requires the last line to be a 'Signed-off-by' line, while B5 requires the last lines to include a trailer block with 'Refs: <TICKET-ID>'. To satisfy both, the 'Signed-off-by' line must appear before the 'Refs' line in the trailer block, making the order critical.

reconciled: Finish the message with a trailer block that contains the line `Refs: <TICKET-ID>`, followed immediately by the sign-off `Signed-off-by: <author name>` on the very last line. Both the trailer and sign-off must appear in that order, with no intervening content.
